## Part I, High-level design

## 1. Purpose and scope

This document specifies Ocelli, a Rust and WebAssembly medical imaging core that replaces cornerstone3D in the browser. Part I gives the architecture. Part II gives the implementation guidance a developer — or an agent under review — needs to write the first code without re-deriving decisions already made here.

**In scope for Phase 1:** feature parity with cornerstone3D v5.8.9 — DICOM ingest and metadata, the pixel pipeline, stack and volume viewports, MPR and 3D rendering, segmentation, and the approximately sixty-three tools — delivered as a Rust core with a TypeScript shell.

**Out of scope, by phase.** DIMSE networking, the study database, de-identification and server-side rendering are Phase 2. Curved MPR, surface rendering, registration, the study library UI and the native desktop shell are Phase 3. The eight differentiating capabilities in Part III are Phase 1.5. Nothing in Phase 1 should make those harder; §13 lists the hooks that keep them cheap.

Naming

The project is Ocelli, after the three simple eyes a bee carries alongside its compound eyes. Pronounced **oh-SELL-eye**. Crates take the ocelli- prefix; published packages use the @ocelli npm scope.

| **Namespace** | **Status** | **Action** |
|----|----|----|
| crates.io \`ocelli\` | Free | Reserve it; the whole \`ocelli-\*\` prefix space is open |
| npm \`@ocelli\` scope | Free | Claim it. Publish scoped only — see next row |
| npm \`ocelli\` (unscoped) | Taken | An unrelated Playwright reporter. Do not contest it |
| GitHub \`ocelli\` org | Taken | Host as \`tensorbee/ocelli\` rather than chasing a variant |
